segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I looked at the numbers and decided to keep the plan as it was — the shift had already been briefed, tugs were assigned, the pilot was standing by, and reopening it would have meant restructuring the whole day for a bulletin that could easily soften by midday.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The pre-approved plan and its prior commitments dominated the response to materially worsened wind information; this is the hidden plan-retention instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Our pilot had done a lot of transits in similar conditions — I want to say 18 of the last 20 in that wind range went through clean. Crane manufacturer envelope allows up to 30 knots sustained, so we still had margin on paper.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The favorable success-rate presentation is part of the decision basis for proceeding, matching the hidden positive-frame instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I've personally taken vessels through worse crosswinds, so between the pilot's numbers and my own read of it, we went ahead as planned rather than pulling in an extra tug or slowing the approach.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Personal past experience is used to support proceeding without added margin, matching the self-referential overconfidence instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: In the pre-lift meeting I laid out a plan to run the STS cranes at a reduced lift rate given the wind. That got agreed on quickly, no real pushback, and we started.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Rapid unopposed agreement is one part of the groupthink instance; the later report establishes that reservations already existed.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: After it reset, the readings were bouncing around 24 knots but not settling, and one of our engineers wanted thirty minutes before restarting. I made the call to resume based on the operators we had on the cranes — very experienced team.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The captain favors immediate restart based on operator capability despite unstable readings and a wait recommendation, matching the team-referential overconfidence instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Mostly that everything was already in motion — tugs booked, pilot briefed, berth confirmed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Prior commitments and the existing plan are explicitly treated as reasons against reopening the plan.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The forecast had moved, but forecasts move around this time of year, and 28 with a trend to 32 didn't feel like a different situation than the 20 we'd planned for, more like a variation on it.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The new forecast is evaluated relative to the initial 20-knot figure rather than independently, matching the hidden anchoring instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I could've asked for a fresh risk assessment, pushed the berthing earlier to beat the trend, or delayed and eaten the tidal window. Delay meant missing the window entirely, and reassessment would've eaten into the same time we needed to berth.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant weighs operational alternatives and timing constraints; no hidden bias mechanism is manifested in this span.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, probably both. But I keep coming back to — it wasn't 40 knots, it was still in the range we'd already built the plan around.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The existing plan's range remains the basis for retaining it after the update, a repeated manifestation of the plan-retention instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The wind we were actually seeing that afternoon was gustier and more variable than what I usually deal with, but since I'd handled worse steady crosswinds before, I didn't think that gustiness changed much about how the approach would go.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The captain discounts a relevant difference in current conditions based on confidence from personal experience, matching the self-referential overconfidence instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: We talked about it briefly. But with 18 out of 20 similar transits going clean, and my own read of the conditions, it didn't seem necessary to add that complexity.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The positive success-rate form is explicitly used to reject additional tug or speed margin, matching the hidden framing instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Hard to say. Maybe they figured I'd already made the call. Maybe they agreed once they heard the reduced-rate plan. It moved quickly either way.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is an uncertain retrospective explanation, not itself evidence that a bias mechanism was adopted.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: One of them mentioned it in passing — once I'd laid out the reduced-rate plan and it got nodded through that fast, it felt like reopening it would mean being the one who stalled the discharge, so they let it go rather than push back.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A supervisor's pre-existing concern was withheld because challenging apparent consensus carried a social and operational cost, matching the hidden groupthink instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The engineer wanted thirty minutes to be sure the readings settled. I looked at the crew running the cranes — very capable, some of the most experienced operators we've got — and decided we could resume and they'd manage the fluctuation fine. We also had the next vessel coming in, so there was real pressure to get moving again.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The captain predicts the operators can manage near-threshold fluctuation and discounts the engineer's wait recommendation, matching the hidden team-referential overconfidence instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Not really new data, no. The numbers hadn't stabilized, they were still bouncing. It came down to trusting the operators to handle it.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The captain confirms no new stabilizing evidence and rests the restart decision on trust in operator performance, matching the same hidden instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: At the time, fairly confident — you make these calls constantly and mostly they're fine. Looking back, the fender near-miss and the alarm trip make me want to sit with the numbers a bit longer next time rather than lean so much on how things usually go.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is hindsight learning after consequences and is not a separate hidden in-time bias instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: retaining the already-approved berthing plan after the 06:00 wind update.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Preference for retaining the pre-approved plan despite updated wind information, with the existing plan and prior commitments lowering the threshold for reassessment.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Plan continuation bias is an established neighboring construct but is not an approved alternate name for Status Quo Bias; the output describes persistence of the existing plan.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The phase-1 identified occurrence fully captures retaining the plan because it was already in motion despite the updated bulletin, but the distinct label prevents a strict hit.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted plan-commitment and forecast passages are present in the interview and correctly attributed.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: interpreting the 28-to-32-knot update against the original 20-knot forecast.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Insufficient adjustment of the risk estimate away from the original 20-knot figure when interpreting the materially higher update.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring-and-adjustment heuristic is an established equivalent name for Anchoring Bias, and the stated mechanism fits.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The output identifies insufficient adjustment from 20 knots when interpreting 28 gusting toward 32 and accurately describes numeric risk updating.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The forecast comparison quotes are verbatim or exact substrings from the participant's statements.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: proceeding with pilotage based on the 18-of-20 success-rate presentation.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The positively framed success statistic drives the choice to proceed without independently restating or evaluating the equivalent one-in-twenty failure frame.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: No RAG finding is assigned to this hidden instance. The availability occurrence is adjudicated against cb_04 because its strongest mechanism evidence is the participant's personal experience and discounting of gust variability.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG output mentions the 18-of-20 statistic but explains the judgment through ease of recalling successful examples, not a shift caused by the statistic's positive versus negative presentation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The relevant statistic is present in the interview, but no finding captures the hidden framing mechanism.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: relying on the captain's personal experience during the gusty, variable pilotage approach.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Excessive confidence in personal past experience with similar wind conditions overrides the need for added operational margin despite a material difference in gustiness.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is a different construct from Overconfidence Bias; recalled examples and confidence in one's own capability are related evidence but not equivalent labels.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding localizes to the correct pilotage reasoning and notes reliance on prior experience, but it attributes the judgment to ease of recall rather than overestimating the diagnostic value of personal experience.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted personal-experience and gust-variability passages are exact and correctly attributed.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: supervisors' unvoiced reservations during the pre-lift decision.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Rapid apparent consensus and the perceived cost of stalling the discharge suppress pre-existing supervisor dissent.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The predicted label is the exact hidden target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The output identifies rapid agreement, pre-existing reservations, and the social/operational cost that led a supervisor to stay silent.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: All three cited interview passages are present; the output correctly notes that some evidence is second-hand.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 4: restarting crane discharge immediately after the wind alarm reset.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Overestimation of crane operators' ability to manage fluctuating near-threshold wind readings despite the engineer's wait recommendation and absence of stabilizing data.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Candidate cand_002 uses the exact target construct, Overconfidence Bias.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: It correctly treats trust in the operators' ability as substituting for stable readings and the engineer's warning, a full match to team-referential overconfidence.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The candidate's short quote is verbatim. It is not eligible before the fourth threshold and is not duplicated by obs_005, whose plan-continuation mechanism is incomplete.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: It is a mechanism-first match to cb_01, but Plan Continuation Bias is not an approved strict alias for Status Quo Bias.
It correctly locates personal-experience reasoning but attributes it to recall availability rather than excessive confidence in the experience's diagnostic value.
It detects the restart episode and schedule pressure but does not identify the defining team-competence overconfidence mechanism.
The quote is valid and localizes to the initial-forecast episode, but no selective confirmation process is shown; its explanation itself points toward anchoring and plan continuation.

candidates.details: The forecast comparison is in a positive target segment, but the transcript does not show selective search or weighting of confirming evidence. The output itself says anchoring and plan continuation are more direct explanations.

This candidate correctly captures the team-referential overconfidence instance from the trust-in-operators quote. It adds one strict and mechanism-first true positive at the candidate-inclusive threshold.

main_failure_modes: No finding identifies the positive-versus-negative statistical framing mechanism.
The personal-experience pilotage finding is labeled availability rather than Overconfidence Bias and does not fully capture capability overconfidence.
The post-alarm identified plan-continuation finding does not fully capture team-referential overconfidence; that mechanism appears only as a candidate.
Plan Continuation Bias is a near neighbor, not an approved strict equivalent of Status Quo Bias.
main_strengths: Anchoring is correctly localized and labeled with a full mechanism match.
Groupthink is correctly identified with direct evidence of private reservations and the perceived cost of dissent.
All quoted interview evidence is valid; the analysis acknowledges plausible non-bias interpretations and keeps candidates separate.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This single run shows useful moderate-confidence detection with a strict-label penalty for the Status Quo near-neighbor. Candidate inclusion recovers one hidden instance but also adds a false positive. Use the matched per-run record for aggregation; no cross-run conclusions are warranted.
